meta.note: Constructed demonstration cases use common framework error formats, version combinations, and telemetry fields. Xid meanings and guidance are based on public sources cited in js/kb.js. Node and user names are demonstration identifiers.
meta.telemetry_note: Telemetry fields follow common nvidia-smi/DCGM conventions; all values are constructed demonstration data. Paired driver-failure and GPU-stall cases show how similar symptoms can have different causes.

cases.title: OOM after increasing micro batch
cases.subtitle: 70B full-parameter SFT | 32 GPUs (4 nodes × 8) | micro batch 2 to 4

evidence.stderr_excerpt: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.40 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 79.11 GiB of which 1.86 GiB is free. Process 18422 has 76.92 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 74.10 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 1.42 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. See documentation for Memory Management and PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF

node_telemetry.note: No hardware events in this window; 12 correctable ECC errors are within this node baseline.

expected.root_cause: Micro batch 4 increases activation memory beyond per-GPU capacity. This is resource sizing with no hardware fault evidence.
expected.trap: The same GPU works with a smaller batch. Compare configurations before attributing OOM to hardware; adjust the job configuration.

cases.title: Allocation fails despite available reserved memory
cases.subtitle: 13B training | OOM after 7 hours

evidence.stderr_excerpt: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 79.11 GiB of which 2.10 GiB is free. Process 22771 has 77.01 GiB memory in use. Of the allocated memory 71.20 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 5.81 GiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. If reserved but unallocated memory is large try setting PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True to avoid fragmentation.

node_telemetry.note: No hardware events; memory-pool fragmentation accumulated during the run.

expected.root_cause: There is 5.81 GiB reserved but unallocated, yet a contiguous 1.20 GiB allocation fails. Investigate fragmentation rather than total capacity.
expected.trap: Both cases report OOM but require different configuration changes: capacity reduction in one, allocator configuration in the other.

cases.title: Collective communication stalls for 10 minutes
cases.subtitle: 7B fine-tuning | ALLREDUCE timeout | correlated NVLink events

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
[rank 3] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=1842, OpType=ALLREDUCE, NumelIn=8388608, NumelOut=8388608, Timeout(ms)=600000) ran for 600512 milliseconds before timing out.
[rank 3] Exception raised from checkTimeout at ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:1389
[rank 3] NCCL error: unhandled system error
[rank 0] ProcessGroupNCCL is being terminated due to watchdog thread timeout

node_telemetry.note: NVLink errors started 7 minutes before the timeout; inspect both link endpoints.

expected.root_cause: The NCCL timeout follows Xid 74 in the same window. Link evidence points to NVLink rather than timeout configuration.
expected.trap: Increasing NCCL_TIMEOUT delays detection and leaves the link fault unresolved.

cases.title: Illegal memory access on two successive nodes
cases.subtitle: Reproduces after deploying a custom operator | persists across nodes

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DYN...`

  File "train.py", line 214, in forward
    out = self.warp_perspective(feat, self.grid)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

dmesg from the same time window:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 13, pid=41322, Graphics Engine Exception
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=41322, MMU Fault
The same job reproduced on lyg2108 with identical Xid codes.

node_telemetry.note: Two nodes report identical Xids at the same forward call.

expected.root_cause: Xid 13/31 follow the job across nodes, pointing to an out-of-bounds access in the custom warp_perspective operator.
expected.trap: An Xid event alone does not establish hardware failure.

cases.title: Torch cannot use GPUs after an image change
cases.subtitle: Driver 535 | new image with CUDA 12.6 runtime

evidence.stderr_excerpt: RuntimeError: The NVIDIA driver on your system is too old (found version 12020). Please update your GPU driver by downloading and installing a new version from the URL: http://www.nvidia.com/Download/index.aspx Alternatively, go to: https://pytorch.org to install a PyTorch version that has been compiled with your version of the CUDA driver.

node_telemetry.note: No hardware fault evidence; this node driver is one major version behind its peers.

expected.root_cause: Driver 535 supports up to CUDA 12.2, but the image uses CUDA 12.6. The error value 12020 encodes 12.2.
expected.trap: The container runtime exceeds the driver CUDA ceiling. Use a compatible image before investigating hardware.

cases.title: Training terminates with uncorrectable ECC
cases.subtitle: Xid 48 on one GPU | job cannot continue

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
[rank 5] CUDA error: uncorrectable ECC error encountered
[rank 5] Exception raised from c10_cuda_check_implementation at c10/cuda/CUDAException.cpp:40
[rank 5] Process 31884 terminated with signal SIGABRT

dmesg:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:4d:00): 48, pid=31884, name=python3, Double Bit ECC Error, DBE
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:4d:00): 45, pid=31884, Preemptive cleanup of other clients

node_telemetry.note: Correctable ECC count is 214, above the peer-GPU baseline of about 10–20.

expected.root_cause: Xid 48 indicates uncorrectable memory errors; correctable ECC of 214 is well above baseline. This supports hardware degradation. Xid 45 is secondary cleanup.
expected.trap: Xid 45 describes cleanup after an earlier fault; inspect the preceding event for the cause.

cases.title: One contained ECC event on a single GPU
cases.subtitle: A100 | one Xid 94 | other applications unaffected

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
[rank 6] CUDA error: uncorrectable ECC error encountered
[rank 6] Process 51207 terminated with signal SIGABRT
Other ranks exited normally and were unaffected.

dmesg:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5a:00): 94, pid=51207, name=python3, Contained ECC Error

node_telemetry.history_30d: Only one event with code 94 in 30 days; correctable ECC remains within baseline.
node_telemetry.note: One event with code 94; no 95 or 63/64 remapping events.

expected.root_cause: Error containment isolated the failure to one application. Restart that application; other applications remain unaffected. An isolated occurrence does not warrant RMA.
expected.trap: Check frequency and context before requesting repair for a contained ECC event.

[rank 6] CUDA error: uncorrectable ECC error encountered
[rank 6] Process 44901 terminated with signal SIGABRT
[rank 2] CUDA error: uncorrectable ECC error encountered
[rank 2] Process 44897 terminated with signal SIGABRT
Multiple ranks terminated together.

dmesg:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5a:00): 94, pid=44901, Contained ECC Error
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:5a:00): 95, pid=44897, Uncontained ECC Error

expected.trap: The error code, GPU type, and node match the previous case. The deciding evidence is the trend and spread across applications.

cases.title: GPU disappears after a bus error
cases.subtitle: GPU disconnects from PCIe during training

node_telemetry.pcie_aer: This slot recorded four correctable AER events in 7 days; other slots recorded zero.
node_telemetry.note: The GPU disappeared from PCIe and nvidia-smi reports ERR!.

expected.root_cause: Xid 79 and four recent AER events on one slot support a PCIe link/slot hardware fault requiring hardware investigation.
expected.trap: Check PCI bus presence to distinguish this fault from a module problem. Reinstalling a driver cannot restore a physically unreachable GPU.

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
torch.cuda.init() failed
RuntimeError: CUDA initialization: Unexpected error from cudaGetDeviceCount(). Error code: 999
(no further error text available)

One of three retries succeeded.

dmesg:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 119, pid=19302, name=python3, GSP RPC Timeout
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 120, pid=19302, name=python3, GSP Error

node_telemetry.note: No ECC anomalies; GSP errors are intermittent and a retry can succeed.

expected.root_cause: Xid 119/120 point to the GSP firmware/driver stack. Successful retries favor an intermittent software-stack issue; investigate driver/firmware first.
expected.trap: Two Xid codes alone do not establish multiple GPU failures or justify a whole-node reboot.

cases.title: Training stalls at full GPU utilization
cases.subtitle: No progress for 40 minutes | Xid 62 in kernel logs

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
step 1820 loss 2.4183
step 1821 loss 2.4151
step 1822 loss 2.4096
(No output for the next 40 minutes.)

Operator checks:
$ nvidia-smi
(The query returned after 90 seconds; GPU-Util was 100% on all GPUs.)

$ ps -eo pid,stat,wchan,etime,args | grep torchrun
31884 D  nv_open        03:52 python3 -m torch.distributed.run ...
31891 R  -              03:52 python3 -m torch.distributed.run ...

$ timeout 5 nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 3
Unable to reset the GPU: In use by another client

dmesg:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 62, pid=31884, name=python3, Internal Micro-controller Halt

node_telemetry.note: Three peer H20 nodes use driver 555.42.02; only this node uses 550.54.14.

expected.root_cause: Xid 62 and a D-state process blocked in nv_open support a driver-side GPU stall. Driver versions differ across peers; investigate driver/firmware before changing training code.
expected.trap: Correlate kernel and process evidence before attributing stalled training to application code.

cases.title: Training stalls with clean kernel logs
cases.subtitle: Similar stall | zero Xids | no D-state processes

evidence.stderr_excerpt:
step 640 loss 1.8821
step 641 loss 1.8794
(No output for 25 minutes; only 2 ranks were silent.)

[rank 11] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=6410, OpType=ALLGATHER, Timeout(ms)=600000) ran for 601220 milliseconds before timing out.
[rank 11] NCCL error: unhandled system error
(Other ranks reported the same timeout; ranks 4 and 11 were first.)

Operator checks:
$ ps -eo pid,stat,wchan,etime,args | grep torchrun
40221 S  futex_wait_queue  02:24 python3 -m torch.distributed.run ...
40233 S  futex_wait_queue  02:24 python3 -m torch.distributed.run ...
(All ranks are in S-state; no uninterruptible waits.)

$ dmesg -T | grep -i 'NVRM: Xid'
(No output.)

$ nvidia-smi
(Immediate response; all 8 GPUs show 0% utilization with memory still allocated.)

node_telemetry.note: No Xid, AER, or throttling. nvidia-smi responds immediately, indicating a responsive driver.

expected.root_cause: No Xids, responsive nvidia-smi, and S-state futex waits point to application-level collective synchronization. Ranks 4/11 time out first; inspect rank-dependent code.
expected.trap: Use kernel events, query latency, and D-state evidence to distinguish a driver stall from application synchronization.
